results.text: Impaired atrioventricular time interaction contributes to tachycardia-induced hemodynamic deterioration: In vivo and in silico hybrid approach. Heart rate (HR) is a major determinant of cardiac output (CO). During tachycardia, adequate left ventricular (LV) filling becomes important; however, excessive tachycardia reduces CO by shortening filling time. [A case of hyponatremia induced by the thiazide-like diuretic indapamide in an elderly woman]. A 72-year-old woman with a history of hypertension who had already been taking calcium channel blockers and angiotensin II receptor blockers was prescribed additional indapamide (1 mg/day) due to inadequate blood pressure control.
